title: GreenGateway authority event delivery v1
description: What the authority-event dispatcher delivers for one journaled evidence row (issue #425 PR 3). A safe projection of identifiers and revisions; the actor is the identifier the evidence row recorded, referenced under the keyed actor.recorded domain, with the actor kind, authentication mode and issuer reference the row records since migration 24 (null for evidence committed before it, and the issuer reference also null for an actor without an issuer). Admin session events sit on the session axis with one revision (1, created by the grant and deleted by the withdrawal) and a null security revision. Since migration 33 the recorded actor on a grant or replacement is the verified login, and rejection or expiry names a system actor. Unauthenticated logout and pre-33 rows retain the session owner's reference and null actor metadata. A service-token issue (journaled since migration 27) sits on the token axis with a null revision before it and revision 1 after it. A Connection create and replace (journaled since migration 28) sit on the connection axis, a create with a null revision before it and revision 1 after it; a replace that changed credential authority is also delivered as credential.binding_change under the same operation ID and security revision, on the credential axis, whose revision before it is 0 when no credential authority was configured, the one place a revision of 0 is delivered. Its resource is the Connection: no binding, secret ID or locator is evidence. Policy, tools and stored policy test suite commits and managed catalog publications (journaled since migration 32) carry their evidence's own operation codes: a document is referenced as the singleton it is, a policy resource on the policy axis, a tools resource on the tools axis, or the stored policy test suite as a policy resource of its own on the policy_tests axis, with the offline import's configuration.import on the axis of the document it activated; a catalog is a catalog resource referenced by its Connection on the catalog axis, without the overlay revision it was compiled from. Each activates a version: a null revision before it when the resource had none, and a strictly greater revision after it, which for a document need not be 1. A document row committed before migration 32 recorded a service-token caller as kind principal with authentication mode service_token, and is delivered as kind service_token, with its issuer canonicalized before it is referenced. Standalone mode has no journal: its dispatcher delivers each SQLite store's own evidence tables, each store its own authority under its own authority_id, so sequence is the row's commit order within its own table (one table per operation family: service_token.*; connection.* and credential.*; secret.*; catalog.*), every standalone record carries a null security revision because a standalone store has no shared one, and a standalone service-token record carries null revisions before and after because the token database keeps no token revision. Local-secret changes (standalone only) sit on the secret axis with the secret's version before and after, except a re-encryption batch, which names no secret and changes no version: it sits on the maintenance axis with null revisions, and its resource reference is derived from the fixed component connection_local_secrets, the local-secret store as a whole. A standalone Connections database's managed catalog and overlay publications are delivered as the journal delivers them: a catalog resource referenced by its Connection on the catalog axis, with the catalog revision before (null for a first catalog) and after. Not the proposed authority_event.v1 contract: the subject reference is not issuer-scoped, older rows and issuer-less actors cannot name an issuer, and only the keyed service-token revoke binds the operation ID to its caller.
